title: The quiet moment between repetitions
note:
The hard part is drawing nothing happening. Every instinct of an illustration model is to give the pair an activity, and any activity here is the wrong picture: this step exists to show a dog who has been asked for nothing and is fine.

Round 33 drew the leash unattached: it hung from the handler's hand, curved across the floor and ended loose beside Lucy, whose collar carried only its tag. The scene text had asked for it clipped to the ring, but mustBeTrue had only asked for a slack curve, so the picture passed the written question while getting the fact wrong — the review question has to carry the part that matters, not the part that is easy to see. An unclipped leash beside a dog is a different picture from a dog on a leash, and this step is about being settled while attached.
scene: The entry hall, a few steps back from the closed charcoal front door. Nothing is being asked of Lucy and nothing is being offered. She stands on all four feet beside the handler, loose and neutral — weight even, tail down and relaxed, head level, looking off toward the middle distance rather than at the handler, at the door, or at the viewer. She is not sitting. The handler stands beside her, upright and easy, both arms hanging at her sides: not reaching, not gesturing, not in the treat pouch, not looking down at Lucy. She looks quietly ahead. THE LEASH IS ATTACHED TO LUCY, and this has to be unmistakable: its metal trigger clip is closed around the D-ring at the FRONT of her collar, under her chin, and the black line runs continuously from that ring — down, into a deep slack curve that touches the floor, and up to the loop the handler holds lightly in one lowered hand. Follow the line with your eye from her collar to her hand without a break. The leash must NOT merely lie on the floor near her with a loose end: an unclipped leash beside a dog is a different picture from a dog on a leash, and this step is about her being settled while attached. Draw the leash with a thin lighter outline where it passes near her coat so it stays readable, and never across her back or shoulders. Neither of them is engaging the other. Background: the lavender wall, one baseboard line, the closed door and the doormat well off to one side. Plenty of empty floor.
mustBeTrue: the leash is visibly clipped to the D-ring at the front of Lucy's collar and runs unbroken from there to the handler's lowered hand, hanging in a slack curve rather than a taut line and never lying loose-ended on the floor; nobody is doing anything — the handler's hands are otherwise empty and at her sides, she is not looking at Lucy and Lucy is not looking at her, no treat and no cue is offered — and Lucy is standing rather than sitting, relaxed and neutral.
